items.problem: A P2P connection that became lost outside `_PEER.poll` raises no peer lost, which differs from `open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/realtime-core.md:97` (`connect_peer` failed). `_start_peer` (line 441) and `_PEER.apply` (`client/godot/core/realtime_core/p2p_peer.gd:70`, `set_remote_description` not `OK`) set `Status.LOST` before `_poll_peer` reads `before`, so `peer.status != before` is false in every later poll, and the object stays in `_peers`. In `Connecting` there is no retry and the match fails at the connect time limit. When an offer with a larger number whose SDP is refused replaces a connected connection, the participant stays `Connected` with no reconnection or `PeerLeftEvent`, and each `send` to that participant is `false` without log

No time limit covers a connection that replaces a connected connection. After `PEER_REJOINED`, the offering side drops the connected connection and starts a new one with `replaces_connected`, and the participant stays `Connected` as `open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/realtime-core.md:126` and `:129` require. `_check_time_limits` (`client/godot/core/realtime_core/realtime_core.gd:524`) measures only `Connecting` and `Disconnected`, and server `PEER_LEFT` does not change participant state. Run path: index 1 rejoins and ends before it answers the new offer; index 0 then has `peer_state`(1) `Connected`, each `send` to it is `false`, and no `PeerDisconnectedEvent` or `PeerLeftEvent` comes unless WebRTC itself reports a failure. The duration is not set by the spec, so the fix needs a spec change

A host in a room that reaches `RealtimeCore.backgroundTimeoutMs` in `Matching` leaves its party in the queue. `_fail_match` calls only `close`, as `open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/realtime-core.md:148` and `:240` say, and `client/godot/core/realtime_core/p2p_realtime_transport.gd:122` sends nothing in a room with no match. Measured in a temporary copy, on this range and on `a0bf92c`: state `None`, `cancel_matching` count 0, `close` count 1. By reading the code, not run: the server keeps the party entry, so the next `join_match` of that host is `ROOM_BUSY` (`server/core/matchmaker/realtime.ts:571`) and a match found for that party is dropped. This range did not change it

A matchmaker lost of the earlier connection ends a `create_room` that already opened a new connection, and nothing closes that connection, so the server keeps a room the client does not know. Reproduced with `RealtimeCore`, `p2p_realtime_transport.gd` and the test matchmaker: a solo `join_match` receives `MATCH_FAILED` and `CLOSE`(`MAINTENANCE`) in one `poll`, and its continuation calls `create_room`. `ROOM_CREATE` goes out on a second connection (accepted 2, closed 1), and `create_room` ends with `ok` `false` and code 3. The next `ROOM_STATE` is discarded and `room_info` stays empty. `leave_room` sends no `ROOM_LEAVE`, and a second `create_room` reuses that connection (`p2p_realtime_transport.gd:183`) and ends `false` on the `ROOM_BUSY` the probe sent. The real server's `ROOM_BUSY` was read at `server/core/matchmaker/realtime.ts:630`, not run. The whole run gives the same values with `realtime_core.gd` of `61bfa19`, so this range did not cause it; `test_room.gd:546` now holds the part in `RealtimeCore`. It answers the question in `## unverified` of `records/1793747414075-update-core-mw1awapne9bcf2.md`. The server stuck state needs a close code that still admits the new connection, such as `RATE_LIMITED` at `realtime.ts:795`, because `MAINTENANCE` and `BANNED` are refused at `HELLO` (`realtime.ts:399`, `:403`). It also needs the `CLOSE` frame read in the same `poll` as the earlier notice and a `create_room` or `join_room` called inside that `poll`

The range makes a client that holds a match send `MATCH_LEAVE` of a second `MATCH_FOUND` and keep the first match, but the server has already removed that connection from the first session when it opened the second (server/core/matchmaker/realtime.ts:931, skills `p2p-signaling` `### match session`). The client then counts as left in both matches while it is still playing the first. Run path: host A and member B play match m1 from a room, which stays after the match (open-game-works-core/skills/server-core/modules/matchmaker.md:154). A leaves m1 and sends `ROOM_START` while B is `Playing`; `room_start` (server/core/matchmaker/realtime.ts:718) does not check whether a member is in a match, so m2 is created. Reproduced on the real `SessionStore` (server/core/p2p-signaling/sessions.ts): opening m2 returned `LEFT` of B in m1, B's `MATCH_LEAVE` of m2 returned `LEFT` of B in m2, B's next `PEER_SIGNAL` was dropped with `not_in_session`, and by the code at server/core/p2p-signaling/sessions.ts:191 its `MATCH_REJOIN` of m1 is `ok` `false` because the index is a left index. Result: B stays `Playing` in m1 with `left_at` written (the case at open-game-works-core/skills/server-core/modules/matchmaker.md:374), so a lost P2P connection in m1 cannot signal or rejoin, and in a `ServerReplay` match of 3 or more B's report is not counted and the judgement does not wait for it (matchmaker.md:184, :186). m2 also holds B as left, and A fails at the connect time limit. The client line follows open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/realtime-core.md:298, and the server side follows matchmaker.md:374, so the two specs together set this result; solving it needs a spec change (e.g. `ROOM_START` refused while a member is bound to a running match session, or the client taking the second match).
